decisions.reason: The standalone supply already powers the full shared 3.3V rail; moving the LEDs onto that rail does not change the stated source-selection or supply behavior.
The LED supply change does not alter the sensor-board module inventory, connector pinouts, or sensor interfaces.
Adding the LEDs as a 3.3V load does not change the established DCDC1 voltage configuration or regulation requirement.
The existing same-message Event removes the shared-load fact but leaves the obsolete SK6812 entry in the 5V rail's powered-load list.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text: The LEDs are now powered from 3.3V instead of 5V. At 3.3V supply the SK6812 data threshold drops to 2.31V, which the ESP32 3.3V output satisfies directly, so no level shifter is needed. The tradeoff is that 3.3V is slightly below the SK6812 datasheet minimum (3.7V), but it works reliably at indicator brightness levels.

decisions.reason: The existing interboard power connectors already carry both 3.3V and 5V, and the source does not change their topology or pinouts.
The LED load moves to an existing AXP2101-powered 3.3V rail without changing the battery, USB, VMID/VSYS, or DCDC1 power-path topology.
A complete same-message MODIFY already records the 3.3V LED supply, direct ESP32 data drive, removal of the level-shifter part, and accepted indicator-brightness condition.
The SK6812 supply and logic change does not affect the SPS30 SEL connection or I2C mode.
The LED rail change does not alter the panel power-button connector or PWRON control behavior.
The source concerns SK6812 power and data levels, not I2C pull-ups, series resistors, cabling, or bus speed.
The LED supply decision does not change the ESP32 BOOT or reset circuitry.
The direct 3.3V LED data drive does not change the selected ESP32-S3 module or its breakout requirement.
